chunks: Ali ibn Ja'far narrated from his brother (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man and a woman, is it permissible for them to introduce medicine while they are fasting? He said, 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.يَسْتَدْخِلَا: to introduce/introduce into (specifically referring to administering medicine)

ai.seo_question: Does taking medicine break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that introducing medicine (such as via inhalation or suppositories) does not invalidate the fast, provided it is not consumed as food or drink. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic distinction between 'consumption' (akl wa shurb) and 'introduction' (idkhal), allowing for medical treatment during Ramadan without breaking the fast. It reflects the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh to accommodate health needs while maintaining the spiritual integrity of fasting.
